what_happened: Two jobs (qc0v and 07nw) finished and landed locally, each with its own pull request (#103 and #104). The flake-fix job (jpe3) was then started on top of their local commits. Its pull request, #105, was squash-merged and carried the content of both earlier jobs into main. #103 and #104 were left open with nothing new to merge. The operator closed them by hand. The job field is null because this was an operator intervention, not a failed job.
cause: Athena treats each job's pull request as independent, and it does not track the dependency when a new job is cut from unmerged local commits of earlier jobs. Nothing reconciles open pull requests against what main contains after a merge. A squash merge hides which earlier commits were included. So there is no lifecycle step for a job whose content arrives through another job's pull request, and the cleanup falls to a person.
prevention: Add a post-merge reconciliation step in code. After any pull request merges, compare each open Athena job pull request's head commits and diff with the new main. If the diff is empty or fully contained in main, close the pull request automatically with a comment that links the merging pull request, and mark the job as landed via that pull request. As a second guard, when a job is cut from another job's unmerged commits, record the dependency and either base its pull request on the earlier job's branch or have it close the earlier pull requests when it merges.
proposed_request: After any Athena pull request is merged to main, automatically check every other open Athena job pull request. If a pull request's changes are already fully contained in main, which includes content that arrived through a squash merge, close it with a comment that links the merging pull request. Mark the matching job as landed via that pull request, and log the closure as an automatic action instead of an operator intervention. Also record which earlier jobs a new job was built on when it is cut from unmerged local commits. Acceptance: in a test repo with two jobs landed locally and a third job cut on top of them, merging the third job's pull request closes the first two pull requests automatically with no manual step. A pull request that still has changes not in main must stay open.
